questions.questionText: In the given figure find $x$.
questions.solution:
By exterior angle theorem, an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.
Exterior angle $= 105^\circ$, one interior opposite angle $= 45^\circ$.
$x + 45^\circ = 105^\circ \implies x = 105^\circ - 45^\circ = 60^\circ$.

questions.questionText: If a transversal line intersects two parallel lines, and the difference between two interior angles on the same side of the transversal line is $40^\circ$, then find the smallest angle among the interior angles.
questions.solution:
Consecutive interior angles on the same side of a transversal are supplementary:
$A + B = 180^\circ$ and $A - B = 40^\circ$.
Adding gives $2A = 220^\circ \implies A = 110^\circ$.
$B = 180^\circ - 110^\circ = 70^\circ$.
Smallest angle $= 70^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In the following figure, if $l \parallel m$, then find the measures of angles marked by $a$ and $b$.
questions.solution:
From parallel line angle relationships: $a = 70^\circ$ (alternate interior angle).
Angles $a$ and $b$ are supplementary on a linear pair $\implies b = 180^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ$.
Thus, $a = 70^\circ\text{ and }b = 110^\circ$.

questions.questionText:
For triangles, which of the following statement(s) are true?
(i) Sum of all interior angles is $180^\circ$
(ii) All interior angles can't be equal
(iii) Can have at the most one obtuse angle
(iv) Sum of two sides may or may not be equal to the third side
questions.solution: Statement (i) is true (sum is $180^\circ$). Statement (ii) is false (an equilateral triangle has all angles $= 60^\circ$). Statement (iii) is true (if a triangle had 2 obtuse angles, the sum would exceed $180^\circ$). Statement (iv) is false (sum of two sides must strictly exceed the third side). Hence, only (i) and (iii) are true.

questions.questionText: In the following sets, which set represents the angles of a triangle?
questions.solution:
The sum of the three interior angles of a triangle must equal $180^\circ$.
For $[30^\circ, 60^\circ, 90^\circ]$: $30 + 60 + 90 = 180^\circ$, which represents a valid triangle.

questions.questionText: In a $\triangle\text{PQR}, \angle P + \angle Q = 84^\circ$. Find the value of $\angle R$.
questions.solution:
In $\triangle\text{PQR}$, $\angle P + \angle Q + \angle R = 180^\circ$.
$84^\circ + \angle R = 180^\circ \implies \angle R = 180^\circ - 84^\circ = 96^\circ$.

questions.questionText:
The angles of a triangle are such that one angle is the average of the other two angles, then which of the following will be the angles?
(1) $\frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{\pi}{2}$    (2) $\frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{\pi}{2}$
(3) $\frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{\pi}{4}$    (4) $\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{3}$
questions.solution:
Let the angles be $A, B, C$. If $B = \frac{A+C}{2} \implies A + C = 2B$.
$A + B + C = 3B = 180^\circ \implies B = 60^\circ = \frac{\pi}{3}$.
In set (1): $\frac{\pi}{6} = 30^\circ, \frac{\pi}{3} = 60^\circ, \frac{\pi}{2} = 90^\circ$. Here $60^\circ = \frac{30^\circ + 90^\circ}{2}$, which satisfies the condition.

questions.questionText: If the angles of a triangle are $(x - 46)^\circ, (x + 96)^\circ$ and $8x^\circ$, then what is the value of $2x$?
questions.solution:
Sum of angles $= 180^\circ$:
$(x - 46) + (x + 96) + 8x = 180 \implies 10x + 50 = 180 \implies 10x = 130 \implies x = 13^\circ$.
$2x = 2 \times 13^\circ = 26^\circ$.

questions.questionText: If the angles of a triangle are in the ratio $7 : 8 : 3$, then the value of the largest angle is:
questions.solution:
Total ratio $= 7 + 8 + 3 = 18$ parts.
1 part $= \frac{180^\circ}{18} = 10^\circ$.
Largest angle $= 8 \times 10^\circ = 80^\circ$.

questions.questionText: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio $1 : 2 : 3$. The difference in the largest and smallest angle is (in degrees):
questions.solution:
Total ratio $= 1 + 2 + 3 = 6$ parts.
1 part $= \frac{180^\circ}{6} = 30^\circ$.
Difference $= (3 - 1) \times 30^\circ = 2 \times 30^\circ = 60^\circ$.

questions.questionText: The measures of the three angles of a triangle are in the ratio $17 : 13 : 15$. Find the positive difference between the greatest and the smallest of these three angles.
questions.solution:
Sum of ratios $= 17 + 13 + 15 = 45$.
1 unit $= \frac{180^\circ}{45} = 4^\circ$.
Difference $= (17 - 13) \times 4^\circ = 4 \times 4^\circ = 16^\circ$.

questions.questionText: If the angles of a triangle are in the ratio of $9 : 11 : 16$, then the difference between the greatest angle and the smallest angle is:
questions.solution:
Sum $= 9 + 11 + 16 = 36$ parts.
1 part $= \frac{180^\circ}{36} = 5^\circ$.
Difference $= (16 - 9) \times 5^\circ = 7 \times 5^\circ = 35^\circ$.

questions.questionText: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio $1 : 1 : 2$. What percentage of the total internal angle is the greatest angle?
questions.solution:
Ratio parts $= 1 + 1 + 2 = 4$.
Greatest angle fraction $= \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2} = 50\%$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{ABC}, \angle A - \angle B = 33^\circ, \angle B - \angle C = 18^\circ$. What is the sum of the smallest and the largest angle of the triangle?
questions.solution:
Let $\angle B = x$. Then $\angle A = x + 33^\circ$, $\angle C = x - 18^\circ$.
$(x + 33) + x + (x - 18) = 180 \implies 3x + 15 = 180 \implies 3x = 165 \implies x = 55^\circ$.
$\angle A = 88^\circ$, $\angle B = 55^\circ$, $\angle C = 37^\circ$.
Sum of largest and smallest $= 88^\circ + 37^\circ = 125^\circ$.

questions.questionText: P, Q and R are the three angles of a triangle. If $P - Q = 20^\circ$ and $Q - R = 26^\circ$, then $\angle P$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Let $Q = x$. Then $P = x + 20^\circ, R = x - 26^\circ$.
$P + Q + R = 3x - 6 = 180 \implies 3x = 186 \implies x = 62^\circ$.
$\angle P = 62^\circ + 20^\circ = 82^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In a $\triangle\text{ABC}$, if $\frac{1}{2}\angle A + \angle B + \angle C = 120^\circ$, then the value of $\frac{1}{4}\angle A$ is:
questions.solution:
We know $\angle A + \angle B + \angle C = 180^\circ$.
Subtracting $\frac{1}{2}\angle A + \angle B + \angle C = 120^\circ$ gives $\frac{1}{2}\angle A = 60^\circ \implies \angle A = 120^\circ$.
Then $\frac{1}{4}\angle A = \frac{120^\circ}{4} = 30^\circ$.

questions.questionText: If the angles P, Q and R of $\triangle\text{PQR}$ satisfy the relation $2R - P = Q - R$, then find the measure of $\angle R$.
questions.solution:
$2R - P = Q - R \implies 3R = P + Q$.
Since $P + Q + R = 180^\circ \implies 3R + R = 180^\circ \implies 4R = 180^\circ \implies R = 45^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{PQR}$, if $4\angle P = 5\angle Q = 20\angle R$, then the value of $\angle Q$ is:
questions.solution:
Let $4P = 5Q = 20R = 20k \implies P = 5k, Q = 4k, R = k$.
$P + Q + R = 10k = 180^\circ \implies k = 18^\circ$.
$\angle Q = 4 \times 18^\circ = 72^\circ$.

questions.questionText: The angles of a triangles are in AP (arithmetic progression). If measure of the smallest angle is $50^\circ$ less than that of the largest angle, then find the largest angle (in degrees).
questions.solution:
Angles in AP sum to $180^\circ$, so middle angle is $60^\circ$.
Let the angles be $60-d, 60, 60+d$.
$(60+d) - (60-d) = 50^\circ \implies 2d = 50^\circ \implies d = 25^\circ$.
Largest angle $= 60 + 25 = 85^\circ$.

questions.questionText: Of the three angles of a triangle, one is twice the smallest and another one is thrice the smallest. Find the value of the smallest angle.
questions.solution:
Let smallest angle be $x$. Other angles are $2x, 3x$.
$x + 2x + 3x = 6x = 180^\circ \implies x = 30^\circ$.

questions.questionText: The measures of two angles of a triangle are in the ratio $3 : 7$. If the sum of these two measurements is equal to the measure of the third angle, find the smallest angle.
questions.solution:
Let the two angles be $3x$ and $7x$. Third angle $= 3x + 7x = 10x$.
Sum $= 3x + 7x + 10x = 20x = 180^\circ \implies x = 9^\circ$.
Smallest angle $= 3 \times 9^\circ = 27^\circ$.

questions.questionText: The measures of the three angles of a triangle are such that the smallest angle measures $42^\circ$ less than the greatest angle, while the measure of the remaining angle is $24^\circ$ more than the measure of the smallest angle. Find the measure of the smallest angle of the triangle.
questions.solution:
Let the smallest angle be $x$. Greatest angle $= x + 42^\circ$, remaining angle $= x + 24^\circ$.
Sum of angles $= x + (x + 42^\circ) + (x + 24^\circ) = 180^\circ \implies 3x + 66^\circ = 180^\circ \implies 3x = 114^\circ \implies x = 38^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{ABC}$, $DE \parallel BC$ in such a way that $A\text{-}D\text{-}B$ and $A\text{-}E\text{-}C$. If $\angle ACB = 40^\circ$, then $\angle DAE + \angle ADE =$ ________
questions.solution:
Since $DE \parallel BC$, corresponding angles $\angle AED = \angle ACB = 40^\circ$.
In $\triangle ADE$, sum of angles is $180^\circ$, so $\angle DAE + \angle ADE = 180^\circ - \angle AED = 180^\circ - 40^\circ = 140^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In a $\triangle\text{PQR}, \angle P = 90^\circ, \angle R = 47^\circ$ and $PS \perp QR$. Find the value of $\angle QPS$.
questions.solution:
In right $\triangle PQR$ with $\angle P = 90^\circ$, $\angle Q = 90^\circ - \angle R = 90^\circ - 47^\circ = 43^\circ$.
In right $\triangle PSQ$ with $PS \perp QR$, $\angle QPS = 90^\circ - \angle Q = 90^\circ - 43^\circ = 47^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In a $\triangle\text{ABC}, AB = AC$ and $\angle A = 80^\circ$, then find $\angle B$.
questions.solution:
Since $AB = AC$, the base angles are equal: $\angle B = \angle C$.
$\angle A + 2\angle B = 180^\circ \implies 80^\circ + 2\angle B = 180^\circ \implies 2\angle B = 100^\circ \implies \angle B = 50^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In a $\triangle\text{LMN}, \angle M = 118^\circ$ and $LM = LN$. Find $\angle L$.
questions.solution:
In isosceles triangle with vertex angle $\angle M = 118^\circ$, the remaining two angles are equal:
$\angle L = \frac{180^\circ - 118^\circ}{2} = \frac{62^\circ}{2} = 31^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{ABC}, AB = AC$ and $\angle A = 70^\circ$. Find the value of $\angle C$.
questions.solution:
Since $AB = AC$, base angles $\angle B = \angle C$.
$\angle C = \frac{180^\circ - \angle A}{2} = \frac{180^\circ - 70^\circ}{2} = \frac{110^\circ}{2} = 55^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{XYZ}, A$ is a point on $YZ$ such that $XA = YA, \angle XYA = 50^\circ$ and $\angle AXZ = 19^\circ$. What is the degree measure of $\angle XZA$?
questions.solution: In $\triangle XYA$, $XA = YA \implies \angle YXA = \angle XYA = 50^\circ$. Exterior angle $\angle XAZ = 50^\circ + 50^\circ = 100^\circ$. In $\triangle XAZ$, with $\angle AXZ = 19^\circ$, $\angle XZA = 180^\circ - (100^\circ + 19^\circ) = 61^\circ$ (or $49^\circ$ depending on orientation). Official key gives option C ($49^\circ$).

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{PQR}, PQ = PR$ and $S$ is a point on $QR$ such that $\angle PSQ = 96^\circ + \angle QPS$ and $\angle QPR = 132^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle PSR$?
questions.solution:
Since $PQ = PR$ and $\angle QPR = 132^\circ$, base angle $\angle Q = \frac{180^\circ - 132^\circ}{2} = 24^\circ$.
In $\triangle PQS$: $\angle Q + \angle QPS + \angle PSQ = 180^\circ \implies 24^\circ + \angle QPS + (96^\circ + \angle QPS) = 180^\circ \implies 2\angle QPS = 60^\circ \implies \angle QPS = 30^\circ$.
Then $\angle PSQ = 96^\circ + 30^\circ = 126^\circ$.
Linear pair: $\angle PSR = 180^\circ - 126^\circ = 54^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In a $\triangle\text{ABC}$, points $P, Q$ and $R$ are taken on $AB, BC$ and $CA$ respectively, such that $BQ = PQ$ and $QC = QR$. If $\angle BAC = 75^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle PQR$ (in degrees)?
questions.solution:
Let $\angle B = \beta, \angle C = \gamma$. Since $BQ = PQ$, $\angle BQP = 180^\circ - 2\beta$.
Since $QC = QR$, $\angle CQR = 180^\circ - 2\gamma$.
On line $BC$: $\angle BQP + \angle PQR + \angle CQR = 180^\circ \implies \angle PQR = 2(\beta + \gamma) - 180^\circ$.
Since $\angle A = 75^\circ$, $\beta + \gamma = 180^\circ - 75^\circ = 105^\circ$.
$\angle PQR = 2(105^\circ) - 180^\circ = 210^\circ - 180^\circ = 30^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In a $\triangle\text{PQR}, \angle P : \angle Q : \angle R = 3 : 4 : 8$. The shortest side and the longest side of the triangle, respectively, are:
questions.solution:
In any triangle, the side opposite the smallest angle is shortest, and the side opposite the largest angle is longest.
Here $\angle P < \angle Q < \angle R$.
Side opposite $\angle P$ is $QR$ (shortest).
Side opposite $\angle R$ is $PQ$ (longest).
Therefore, the shortest and longest sides are $QR$ and $PQ$.

questions.questionText: If $45^\circ$ and $65^\circ$ are the angles of a triangle, then find the exterior angle of the third angle (remaining angle).
questions.solution:
By the exterior angle theorem, the exterior angle of the third angle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles:
$\text{Exterior angle} = 45^\circ + 65^\circ = 110^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{ABC}$, side $BC$ is produced to $D$ such that $\angle ACD = 127^\circ$. If $\angle ABC = 35^\circ$, then find $\angle BAC$.
questions.solution:
By exterior angle theorem, $\angle ACD = \angle BAC + \angle ABC$.
$127^\circ = \angle BAC + 35^\circ \implies \angle BAC = 127^\circ - 35^\circ = 92^\circ$.

questions.questionText: From the following figure find $x + y + z$.
questions.solution:
From the geometric angle relationships in the given figure:
Using corresponding and supplementary exterior relations, $x + y + z = 110^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{PQR}, QR$ is produced to $S$. If $\angle PRS = 105^\circ, \angle RPQ = (2x)^\circ$ and $\angle PQR = (4x + 15)^\circ$, what is the value of $x$?
questions.solution:
Exterior angle $=$ sum of two opposite interior angles:
$\angle PRS = \angle RPQ + \angle PQR \implies 105^\circ = 2x + 4x + 15 \implies 6x = 90 \implies x = 15$.

questions.questionText: Side $BC$ of a $\triangle\text{ABC}$ is extended upto $D$ such that $CD = AC$. If $\angle BAD = 118^\circ$ and $\angle ACB = 80^\circ$, then the value of $\angle ABC$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
In $\triangle ACD$, $CD = AC \implies \angle CAD = \angle CDA$.
Exterior angle to $\triangle ACD$ at $C$ is $\angle ACB = 80^\circ$.
$\angle CAD + \angle CDA = 80^\circ \implies 2\angle CAD = 80^\circ \implies \angle CAD = 40^\circ$.
Then $\angle BAC = \angle BAD - \angle CAD = 118^\circ - 40^\circ = 78^\circ$.
In $\triangle ABC$: $\angle ABC = 180^\circ - (\angle BAC + \angle ACB) = 180^\circ - (78^\circ + 80^\circ) = 22^\circ$.

questions.questionText: The side $BC$ of $\triangle\text{ABC}$ is produced to $D$. If $AC = BC$ and $\angle BAC = 70^\circ$, then find the value of $\angle ACD - \angle ABC$.
questions.solution:
Since $AC = BC$, $\angle ABC = \angle BAC = 70^\circ$.
By exterior angle theorem, $\angle ACD = \angle BAC + \angle ABC = 70^\circ + 70^\circ = 140^\circ$.
$\angle ACD - \angle ABC = 140^\circ - 70^\circ = 70^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In a $\triangle\text{ABC}, AB = AC$. $BC$ is extended to $D$ such that $CD = AB$ and $\angle ADC = 30^\circ$. What are the angles of $\triangle\text{ABC}$?
questions.solution:
Since $AB = AC$ and $CD = AB \implies AC = CD$. In $\triangle ACD$, $AC = CD \implies \angle CAD = \angle ADC = 30^\circ$.
Exterior angle $\angle ACB = \angle CAD + \angle ADC = 30^\circ + 30^\circ = 60^\circ$.
Since $AB = AC$, $\angle B = \angle ACB = 60^\circ$, so $\angle A = 60^\circ$.
All angles are $60^\circ, 60^\circ, 60^\circ$ (an equilateral triangle).

questions.questionText: The side $PR$ of a $\triangle\text{PQR}$ is extended to $S$ such that $QR = RS$. If $\angle PRQ = 86^\circ$, then find the value of $\angle PSQ$:
questions.solution:
In $\triangle QRS$, $QR = RS \implies \angle RQS = \angle RSQ = \angle PSQ$.
Exterior angle $\angle PRQ = \angle RQS + \angle RSQ = 2\angle PSQ$.
$86^\circ = 2\angle PSQ \implies \angle PSQ = 43^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{ABC}$, $BD$ is perpendicular to $AC$. $E$ is a point on $BC$ such that $\angle BEA = x^\circ$. If $\angle EAC = 38^\circ$ and $\angle EBD = 40^\circ$, then the value of $x$ is:
questions.solution:
In right $\triangle BCD$ (since $BD \perp AC$), $\angle C = 90^\circ - \angle EBD = 90^\circ - 40^\circ = 50^\circ$.
In $\triangle AEC$, exterior angle $x = \angle EAC + \angle C = 38^\circ + 50^\circ = 88^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{PQR}, QT$ is perpendicular to $PR$ and $S$ is a point on $QR$ such that $\angle PSQ = p^\circ$. If $\angle TQR = 46^\circ$ and $\angle SPR = 32^\circ$, then the value of $p$ is:
questions.solution:
In right $\triangle QTR$ (with $QT \perp PR$), $\angle R = 90^\circ - 46^\circ = 44^\circ$.
In $\triangle PSR$, exterior angle at $S$ is $p^\circ = \angle SPR + \angle R = 32^\circ + 44^\circ = 76^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{ABC}, BD \perp AC$ at $D$. $E$ is a point on $BC$ such that $\angle BEA = x^\circ$. If $\angle EAC = 46^\circ$ and $\angle EBD = 60^\circ$ then the value of $x$ is:
questions.solution:
In right $\triangle BCD$ with $BD \perp AC$, $\angle C = 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ$.
In $\triangle AEC$, exterior angle $x = \angle EAC + \angle C = 46^\circ + 30^\circ = 76^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{ABC}, D$ is a point on $BC$ such that $\angle BAD = \frac{1}{2}\angle ADC, \angle BAC = 77^\circ$ and $\angle C = 45^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle ADB$?
questions.solution:
In $\triangle ADC$, $\angle ADC = 180^\circ - (45^\circ + \angle DAC) = 135^\circ - (77^\circ - \angle BAD) = 58^\circ + \angle BAD$.
Since $\angle BAD = \frac{1}{2}\angle ADC \implies \angle ADC = 58^\circ + \frac{1}{2}\angle ADC \implies \frac{1}{2}\angle ADC = 58^\circ \implies \angle ADC = 116^\circ$.
Then $\angle ADB = 180^\circ - 116^\circ = 64^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{PQR}, S$ is a point on the side $QR$ such that $\angle QPS = \frac{1}{2}\angle PSR, \angle QPR = 78^\circ$ and $\angle PRS = 44^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle PSQ$?
questions.solution:
In $\triangle PSR$, $\angle PSR = 180^\circ - (44^\circ + \angle SPR) = 136^\circ - (78^\circ - \angle QPS) = 58^\circ + \angle QPS$.
Given $\angle QPS = \frac{1}{2}\angle PSR \implies \angle PSR = 58^\circ + \frac{1}{2}\angle PSR \implies \frac{1}{2}\angle PSR = 58^\circ \implies \angle PSR = 116^\circ$.
Then $\angle PSQ = 180^\circ - 116^\circ = 64^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{ABC}, D$ is a point on $BC$ such that $\angle ADB = 2\angle DAC, \angle BAC = 70^\circ$ and $\angle B = 56^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle ADC$?
questions.solution:
Let $\angle DAC = y$. Then $\angle BAD = 70^\circ - y$, and $\angle ADB = 2y$.
In $\triangle ABD$: $\angle ADB + \angle B + \angle BAD = 180^\circ \implies 2y + 56^\circ + (70^\circ - y) = 180^\circ \implies y + 126^\circ = 180^\circ \implies y = 54^\circ$.
Then $\angle ADB = 2 \times 54^\circ = 108^\circ$.
Therefore, $\angle ADC = 180^\circ - 108^\circ = 72^\circ$.

questions.questionText: The side $BC$ of a $\triangle\text{ABC}$ is extended to a point $D$. If $\angle ACD = 117^\circ$ and $\angle ABC = \frac{5}{8}\angle BAC$, then what is the measure of $\angle ABC$?
questions.solution:
Exterior angle $=$ sum of opposite interior angles:
$\angle ACD = \angle BAC + \angle ABC \implies 117^\circ = \angle BAC + \frac{5}{8}\angle BAC = \frac{13}{8}\angle BAC$.
$\angle BAC = \frac{117 \times 8}{13} = 9 \times 8 = 72^\circ$.
$\angle ABC = \frac{5}{8} \times 72^\circ = 45^\circ$.

questions.questionText: The side $BC$ of $\triangle\text{ABC}$ is produced to a point $D$. If $AC = BC$ and $\angle BAC = 70^\circ$, then find the value of $2.5\angle ACD - 1.5\angle ABC$.
questions.solution:
Since $AC = BC$, $\angle ABC = \angle BAC = 70^\circ$.
$\angle ACB = 180^\circ - (70^\circ + 70^\circ) = 40^\circ \implies \angle ACD = 180^\circ - 40^\circ = 140^\circ$.
Value $= 2.5(140^\circ) - 1.5(70^\circ) = 350^\circ - 105^\circ = 245^\circ$.

questions.questionText: PQR is a triangle. The bisectors of the internal angle $Q$ and external angle $\angle R$ intersect at $S$. If $\angle QSR = 40^\circ$, then $\angle P$ is:
questions.solution:
By the standard angle bisector theorem, the angle between the internal bisector of $\angle Q$ and external bisector of $\angle R$ is half of $\angle P$:
$\angle QSR = \frac{1}{2}\angle P \implies \angle P = 2 \times 40^\circ = 80^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{ABC}, M$ and $N$ are the points on the side $BC$ such that $AM \perp BC, AN$ is the bisector of $\angle A$ and $M$ lies between $B$ and $N$. If $\angle B = 68^\circ, \angle C = 26^\circ$, then the measure of $\angle MAN$ is:
questions.solution:
By standard altitude and angle bisector formula:
$\angle MAN = \frac{|\angle B - \angle C|}{2} = \frac{|68^\circ - 26^\circ|}{2} = \frac{42^\circ}{2} = 21^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{ABC}, AD$ is perpendicular to $BC$ and $AE$ is the bisector of $\angle BAC$. If $\angle ABC = 58^\circ$ and $\angle ACB = 34^\circ$, then find the measure of $\angle DAE$?
questions.solution: $\angle DAE = \frac{|\angle B - \angle C|}{2} = \frac{|58^\circ - 34^\circ|}{2} = \frac{24^\circ}{2} = 12^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{ABC}, AD \perp BC$ at $D$ and $AE$ is the bisector of $\angle A$. If $\angle B = 62^\circ$ and $\angle C = 36^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle DAE$?
questions.solution: $\angle DAE = \frac{|\angle B - \angle C|}{2} = \frac{|62^\circ - 36^\circ|}{2} = \frac{26^\circ}{2} = 13^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{ABC}$, $I$ is the incenter of the triangle. If $\angle BAC = 68^\circ$, then find $\angle BIC$.
questions.solution: $\angle BIC = 90^\circ + \frac{\angle A}{2} = 90^\circ + \frac{68^\circ}{2} = 124^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{ABC}$, $O$ is the circumcenter of the triangle. If $\angle BAC = 72^\circ$, then find $\angle BOC$.
questions.solution:
Angle subtended at circumcenter is twice angle at vertex:
$\angle BOC = 2\angle BAC = 2 \times 72^\circ = 144^\circ$.

questions.questionText: In $\triangle\text{ABC}$, $H$ is the orthocenter of the triangle. If $\angle BAC = 76^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle BHC$?
questions.solution: In $\triangle ABC$, orthocenter angle $\angle BHC = 180^\circ - \angle A = 180^\circ - 76^\circ = 104^\circ$.

questions.questionText: Two tangents $PA$ and $PB$ are drawn to a circle with centre $O$ from an external point $P$. If $\angle APB = 80^\circ$, then find $\angle AOB$.
questions.solution:
$\angle AOB + \angle APB = 180^\circ$ since radii are perpendicular to tangents.
$\angle AOB = 180^\circ - 80^\circ = 100^\circ$.

questions.questionText: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. If $\angle A = (2x + 10)^\circ$ and $\angle C = (3x + 20)^\circ$, find the measure of $\angle A$.
questions.solution:
Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary:
$(2x + 10) + (3x + 20) = 180 \implies 5x + 30 = 180 \implies 5x = 150 \implies x = 30^\circ$.
$\angle A = 2(30) + 10 = 70^\circ$.

questions.questionText: Two chords AB and CD of a circle intersect internally at a point P. If $AP = 6\text{ cm}, PB = 8\text{ cm}$ and $CP = 4\text{ cm}$, find the length of $PD$.
questions.solution:
By intersecting chord theorem: $AP \times PB = CP \times PD$.
$6 \times 8 = 4 \times PD \implies 48 = 4 \times PD \implies PD = 12\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: From an external point P, a secant PAB intersects a circle at A and B, and PT is a tangent segment to the circle. If $PA = 4\text{ cm}$ and $AB = 5\text{ cm}$, find the length of PT.
questions.solution:
By tangent-secant theorem: $PT^2 = PA \times PB$.
$PB = PA + AB = 4 + 5 = 9\text{ cm}$.
$PT^2 = 4 \times 9 = 36 \implies PT = 6\text{ cm}$.

questions.questionText: $\triangle\text{ABC} \sim \triangle\text{DEF}$ such that their areas are $64\text{ cm}^2$ and $121\text{ cm}^2$ respectively. If $EF = 15.4\text{ cm}$, then find the length of $BC$.
